R1D-bear-backcountry-0002.name: By Taaltz Creek
R1D-bear-backcountry-0002.pressureWhy: More than 5 km from a drivable road (estimate).
R1D-bear-backcountry-0002.parkWhat: pull off on an unnamed gravel road

evidence.t: Cutblock harvested 2016 (10 years old), 90 m N: cutblocks and logging road edges green up first in spring (65%) and grow berries for the fall feed (lesson: Black bear).
S facing slope, 10 degrees: grassy south facing slopes are spring bear food (90%, lesson: Black bear Masterclass 5).
Taaltz Creek 110 m SE: stream sides and skunk cabbage swamps are spring food, and bears forage on berries and spawning fish in fall (90%, lesson: Black bear Masterclass 5).
1 km or more from pavement and 2 km from a town: bears near people feed more at night (75%, lesson: Black bear Masterclass 6).

seasonRows.notes: bag 2; Bow Only; no bow only season on the Gulf Islands in MU 1-1 (except Gabriola Island), in zone B of MU 1-5 (Map A12) or on Denman and Hornby Islands (MU 1-6)

plan: Drive: from City of Campbell River, about 202 km (straight line times 1.3, estimate).
Park: 51.12282, -126.66142, pull off on an unnamed gravel road. Map links below.
Walk: 7.1 km SE, cross country, no trail mapped. Climb about 1,232 m, about 265 min at 3 km/h.
Camp: flat ground 140 m SE of the spot at 45 m (51.06354, -126.62051). Water: Taaltz Creek 20 m N (estimate).

Hunt: black bear, Apr, May, June, Aug, Sept, Oct, Nov, Dec (season rows). Glass berry slopes, cutblocks and road edges at dawn and the last 2 hours of light, wind in your face (Tip). A bear under 2 years old and any bear with it are closed (99%, synopsis page 11).
Use: your .308 Winchester with a 150 to 180 grain expanding bullet (Tip).
Legal: MU (Management Unit) 1-14, Region 1. Season rows below. Study aid only. The official regulations are the law.
Verify: Candidate, scout it first. Check posted signs. Private land can be unsigned. Data dates: roads 2026-10-16, private land 2026-10-09, closures 2026-10-16.
